proposals.before: On the first day of the fifth month, dingchou, the former Tang chancellors Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were made vice directors of the Secretariat, and Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju became vice director of the Chancellery; all held the rank of co-equal grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.after: On the first day of the fifth month, dingchou, the former Tang chancellors Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were made vice directors of the Chancellery (Menxia), and Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju became vice director of the Secretariat (Zhongshu); all held the rank of co-equal grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.reason: Chinese assigns 門下侍郎 to Zhang Wenwei and Yang She and 中書侍郎 to Xue Yiju; the idiomatic English reverses these two offices.

decisions.reason: The literal field has the same office reversal as the idiomatic: Chinese 門下侍郎 goes to Zhang and Yang, 中書侍郎 to Xue. The proposed wording corrects that without other changes.

decisions.reason: The focus unit has 皇高祖黯, and the next units are 曾祖茂琳, 祖信, and 考诚: 高祖 is the generation above 曾祖, so English “great-grandfather” understates the kinship. “High ancestor (gaozu)” correctly marks that generation.
Focus unit 曾祖茂琳 is great-grandfather in the 高祖–曾祖–祖–考 sequence; idiomatic “grandfather” collapses him with 祖信 in the next sentence. The proposed “great-grandfather/great-grandmother” matches 曾祖.
Literal English likewise renders 曾祖 as grandfather. Changing to great-grandfather/great-grandmother corrects the generation without altering titles or names.
Focus unit states 于兢為中書侍郎: Zhongshu is the Secretariat, not the Chancellery. The proposed idiomatic wording correctly names that office while leaving Zhang Ce’s appointment unchanged.
